claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is treated as a chemically disordered bulk crystal.
A combined large-supercell DFT, machine-learning interatomic-potential, and KKR-CPA framework can calculate lattice and electronic thermal conductivities independently.
Machine-learning-enhanced interatomic potentials enable efficient extraction of anharmonic force constants for HfNbTaTiZr.
Local force-constant and chemical-disorder fluctuations produce phonon scattering that must be represented by models more complex than simple analytical disorder models.
Accurate DFT-derived local force constants capture anharmonic and disorder-induced phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
KKR-CPA calculations capture chemical-disorder-induced electronic scattering or broadening.
Chemical disorder can suppress electronic thermal conductivity by increasing electrical resistivity.
Short-range order mediates changes in phonon lifetimes and electron-scattering rates in HfNbTaTiZr.
One weight percent oxygen introduces local scattering centers that alter phonon lifetimes and electron-scattering rates.
Separating the lattice and electronic calculations avoids conflating the two heat-transport channels.
The proposed framework should outperform conventional Debye and simplified analytical approaches because it represents atomic-scale disorder and separates electronic from lattice transport.
In defect-free HfNbTaTiZr, lattice thermal conductivity will be 30–50% lower than conventional Debye-model estimates.
The predicted lattice-conductivity reduction can be obtained with ±10% relative uncertainty.
Adding 1 wt.% oxygen will cause an additional 15–20% reduction in lattice thermal conductivity.
Below 200 K, the lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions will be nearly equal.
At temperatures of at least 300 K, electronic thermal conductivity will decrease approximately as T^(-1).
At temperatures of at least 300 K, lattice thermal conductivity will saturate and become weakly temperature dependent.
The model is applicable to defect-minimized and controlled 1 wt.% oxygen-doped HfNbTaTiZr specimens from below 200 K through 1200 K.
Extrinsic defects other than controlled oxygen incorporation may not be adequately captured by the model.
The ±10% uncertainty estimate is based on existing computational benchmarks.
